newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITV network losing ground to cable, satellite.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITV network losing ground to cable, satellite.

text.p: Britain's largest commercial television network, ITV, is losing ground to cable and satellite channels, while the BBC is maintaining its audience, according to a report released on Tuesday.

In addition, ITV continues to attract an increasingly older and more downmarket viewing audience, the Institute of Practitioners in Advertising (IPA), a trade group, said in its report, Trends in Television Viewing.
The IPA said cable and satellite channels are gaining the younger television viewers.

Younger and more upmarket viewers tend to be the most heavily sought-after by advertisers due to their higher spending patterns and greater willingness to try new products. Channel 5, Britain's fifth terrestrial television station and third commercial network, which is due to launch in late March, has said its programming will be aimed at younger viewers.

In the 1996 fourth quarter ITV's audience share dropped to 35.1 percent from 37.6 percent a year earlier, the IPA said. Cable and satellite channels, meanwhile, claimed a 10.7 percent audience share in the 1996 fourth quarter compared to 8.8 percent in the year-ago period.
BBC1, the flagship non-commercial channel, paid for by compulsory licence fees, saw its audience share unchanged in the 1996 fourth quarter from the prior year at 32.6 percent, the IPA said.
The IPA said over the four-year period from 1992 to 1996 BBC1 retained a share of about 32 to 33 percent, while ITV saw its audience share fall to about 35 percent in 1995 from 39 percent in 1993.

"This decline has occurred mainly during the last two years and would appear to indicate that the growth in viewing to satellite and cable channels is happening at the expense of ITV more than other channels," the IPA said.
BBC2 and Channel 4, both of which are aimed at niche markets as opposed to the mass market approach of BBC1 and ITV, are seeing fairly stable audiences.

BBC2 had a 10.9 percent audience share in the 1996 fourth quarter compared to 11.1 percent in the 1995 period. Channel 4, a commercial channel whose remit is to cater to an alternative audience, had a 10.6 percent share in the 1996 fourth quarter compared to 8.8 percent in the 1995 quarter.

The 1996 fourth quarter changes in audience viewing patterns were consistent with the trends established throughout the year, with ITV posting slight drops each quarter from the prior year as cable and satellite channels continually made inroads.

ITV's audience share in the first, second and third 1996 quarters, respectively, was 36.5 percent, 34.4 percent and 34.3 percent, compared to 38.0 percent, 36.9 percent and 36.3 percent in the 1995 quarters, the IPA said.

Cable and satellite channels in the 1996 first, second and third quarters, respectively, had audience share of 9.3 percent, 9.9 percent and 10.5 percent compared to 7.7 percent, 8.5 percent and 9.1 percent in the 1995 comparative quarters, the IPA reported.
For the 1996 fourth quarter ITV's audience breakdown by age group included 34.1 percent of 16- to 34-year-olds, 34.4 percent of 35 to 54 years, and 37.3 percent of 55 and over, the IPA said.
